events.title: Mount Vesuvius Eruption (Pompeii)
events.description: The AD 79 eruption that buried Pompeii in ash, preserving Roman life in remarkable detail. Thousands perished.

events.title: Black Death in Europe
events.description: The Black Death (1346-1353) was a devastating global epidemic of bubonic plague that killed up to 50 million people in Europe, about 60% of the population. It profoundly changed European society, leading to economic restructuring and religious upheaval.

events.title: Assassination of Louis I, Duke of Orléans
events.description: Louis I, Duke of Orléans, was assassinated on 23 November 1407 in Paris, France. The assassination occurred during the power struggles between two factions attempting to control the regency of France during the reign of King Charles VI, who was seen as unfit to rule due to his mental illness. One faction was led by Louis, the king's younger brother, and Queen Isabeau of Bavaria, Charles' wife. events.title: Tower of London executions
events.description: The Tower of London was the site of numerous executions over 900 years. Victims include Anne Boleyn (1536), Catherine Howard (1542), Lady Jane Grey (1554), and Sir Thomas More.

events.title: Roanoke Colony disappearance
events.description: The Roanoke Colony vanished from Roanoke Island, North Carolina in the 1590s. When Governor John White returned from England in 1590, the 115 colonists had disappeared without a trace. The only clue was the word 'Croatoan' carved into a post.

events.title: Execution of Charles I of England
events.description: Charles I, King of England, Scotland and Ireland, was publicly executed on 30 January 1649 outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall, London, following his conviction for treason by the Rump Parliament. His execution was a culmination of the English Civil War.

events.title: Great Plague of London
events.description: The Great Plague of 1665 killed an estimated 100,000 people, nearly a quarter of London's population. The bubonic plague epidemic peaked in September 1665 before the Great Fire of 1666 helped eradicate the rat-infested conditions.

events.title: Great Fire of London
events.description: The 1666 conflagration that swept through London, destroying St. Paul's and 13,200 houses over four days.

events.title: Salem Witch Trials
events.description: The 1692-1693 witch trials in colonial Massachusetts. 20 executed. A cautionary tale about mass hysteria.

events.title: Boston Massacre
events.description: The Boston Massacre on March 5, 1770 saw British soldiers fire into a crowd of colonists, killing five. It became a rallying cry for the American Revolution.

events.title: Great New Orleans Fire (1788)
events.description: The Great New Orleans Fire of March 21, 1788 destroyed 856 of the city's 1,100 buildings on Good Friday. The fire started at the home of a Spanish military treasurer and raged for five hours. The subsequent Spanish rebuilding gave the French Quarter its distinctive architecture.

events.title: Sainte-Pélagie Prison
events.description:
Sainte-Pélagie was a prison in Paris, in active use from 1790 to 1899. It was founded earlier than that, however, in 1662, as place for "repentant girls" and later "debauched women and girls." The former Parisian prison was located between the current group of buildings bearing No. 56 Rue de la Clef with Rue du Puits-de-l'Ermite in the 5th arrondissement of Paris at the old Place Sainte-Pélagie.
The penal structure held many noted prisoners during the French Revolution, with Madame Roland, Grace

events.title: Execution of Louis XVI
events.description: King Louis XVI of France was executed by guillotine on January 21, 1793, in the Place de la Révolution (now Place de la Concorde) in Paris. His execution marked a turning point in the French Revolution and ended over 1,000 years of continuous French monarchy.

events.title: Prison de la Santé
events.description: La Santé Prison is one of the most famous prisons in Paris, operational since 1867. It has housed many notable inmates including French Resistance members, gangsters, and terrorists. It's the only prison still operating within Paris city limits.

events.title: Fires in the Paris Commune
events.description: During the Paris Commune of 1871, Communards set fire to numerous government buildings and monuments, including the Tuileries Palace and the Hôtel de Ville, as government troops recaptured the city in one of the bloodiest urban conflicts in French history.

events.title: Great Chicago Fire
events.description: The 1871 fire that destroyed 3.3 square miles of Chicago, leaving over 100,000 homeless. Legend says Mrs. O'Leary's cow started it.

events.title: Los Angeles Chinese massacre of 1871
events.description: The Chinese massacre of 1871 was a racially motivated riot in Los Angeles on October 24 that killed at least 18 Chinese immigrants. A mob of about 500 white men rampaged through Chinatown, looting and hanging victims. It remains one of the largest mass lynchings in American history.

events.title: Battle of Liberty Place
events.description: The Battle of Liberty Place, or Battle of Canal Street, was an attempted insurrection by the Crescent City White League against the Reconstruction Era Louisiana Republican state government on September 14, 1874, in New Orleans, which was the capital of Louisiana at the time. Five thousand members of the White League, a paramilitary organization made up largely of Confederate veterans, fought against the outnumbered racially integrated New Orleans Metropolitan Police and state militia. events.title: Jack the Ripper Murders
events.description: The infamous unsolved serial murders of at least five women in Whitechapel, London, 1888. The killer mutilated his victims and was never identified.

events.title: Lizzie Borden Murders
events.description: The 1892 ax murders of Andrew and Abby Borden in Fall River, MA. Lizzie Borden was acquitted. The case remains a notorious unsolved mystery.

events.title: Windsor Hotel fire
events.description: The Windsor Hotel fire on March 17, 1899 in New York City killed 45 people, mostly women and children trapped on upper floors. The luxury hotel's lack of fire escapes and locked exits turned a small fire into one of the worst hotel disasters in American history.

events.title: Iroquois Theatre fire
events.description: The Iroquois Theatre fire in Chicago on December 30, 1903, killed 602 people in one of the deadliest single-building fires in US history. The theatre was packed with 1,700 people for a matinee performance of 'Mr. Blue Beard' when a spotlight ignited scenery. Panic, locked exits, and inadequate fire safety caused the horrific death toll.

events.title: Charing Cross roof collapse
events.description: On 5 December 1905, the iron-and-glass overall arched roof of Charing Cross railway station in London collapsed during maintenance work, killing six people and injuring several others.

events.title: 1906 San Francisco Earthquake
events.description: The devastating 1906 earthquake that destroyed 80% of San Francisco. Fires burned for days. Over 3,000 died.

events.title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
events.description: The 1911 Manhattan factory fire that killed 146 garment workers. Victims jumped from windows to escape flames. Led to major safety reforms.

events.title: Sinking of the RMS Titanic
events.description: The 1912 sinking of the RMS Titanic after striking an iceberg. Over 1,500 died in one of history's deadliest peacetime maritime disasters.

events.title: RMS Lusitania Sinking
events.description: The 1915 sinking by a German U-boat off Ireland. 1,198 died. Turned opinion against Germany in WWI.

events.title: Murder of the Romanov family
events.description: The Russian Imperial Romanov family — Tsar Nicholas II, his wife Alexandra, and their five children — were executed by Bolshevik revolutionaries on July 17, 1918 in Yekaterinburg, Russia. Their murders ended the 300-year-old Romanov dynasty.

events.title: Spanish flu pandemic of 1918
events.description: The 1918 influenza pandemic infected about one-third of the world's population and killed an estimated 50 million people. It was one of the deadliest pandemics in human history, killing more people than World War I.

events.title: Wingfoot Air Express crash
events.description: The Wingfoot Air Express crash occurred on July 21, 1919, when a dirigible crashed through the skylight of the Illinois Trust and Savings Bank in Chicago, igniting a fire that killed 13 people and injured 27. The burning hydrogen from the airship caused the bank to become an inferno.

events.title: Hinterkaifeck Murders
events.description: The unsolved 1922 mass murder of six at a remote Bavarian farmstead. The killer was never found. Bizarre footprints in the snow and strange noises heard days before.

events.title: Hotel Royal fire
events.description: The Hotel Royal fire in New York City on August 3, 1926 killed 15 people and injured 30. The fire started in a ground-floor restaurant and spread rapidly due to open stairways. Many guests jumped from windows to escape the flames. The tragedy led to stricter fire safety codes.

events.title: St. Valentine's Day Massacre
events.description: The 1929 murder of seven North Side Gang members in a Chicago garage. Ordered by Al Capone during Prohibition-era gang wars.

events.title: Holodomor genocide
events.description: The Holodomor was a man-made famine in Soviet Ukraine from 1932-33 that killed 3-5 million people. The starvation was deliberately inflicted by Stalin's regime to suppress Ukrainian independence.

events.title: Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary
events.description: Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary on Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay operated from 1934 to 1963. It housed notorious criminals including Al Capone and Robert Stroud. The 1962 escape attempt by Frank Morris and the Anglin brothers inspired the film 'Escape from Alcatraz'.

events.title: Hindenburg Disaster
events.description: The 1937 crash and fire of the zeppelin Hindenburg at Lakehurst, NJ. 36 died. Ended passenger airship travel.

events.title: Nanking Massacre
events.description: The Nanking Massacre of 1937-38 saw Japanese troops kill an estimated 300,000 Chinese civilians and POWs. Tens of thousands of women were raped during the six-week rampage.

events.title: Auschwitz concentration camp
events.description: Auschwitz-Birkenau was Nazi Germany's largest extermination camp, where over 1.1 million people were systematically murdered between 1940 and 1945. The ultimate symbol of the Holocaust.

events.title: Dunkirk evacuation
events.description: The Dunkirk evacuation of May-June 1940 rescued over 338,000 Allied soldiers trapped in northern France. The 'Miracle of Dunkirk' used a flotilla of military and civilian boats.

events.title: London Blitz
events.description: The Blitz was a German bombing campaign against the UK from September 1940 to May 1941. Over 40,000 civilians were killed and over a million houses destroyed in London alone.

events.title: Pearl Harbor Attack
events.description: The 1941 Japanese surprise attack on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. 2,403 Americans killed. Led to US entry into WWII.

events.title: Battle of Stalingrad
events.description: The Battle of Stalingrad (1942-43) was the deadliest battle in human history with an estimated 2 million total casualties. The Nazi defeat marked a turning point in World War II.

events.title: D-Day landings
events.description: The Normandy landings on June 6, 1944 were the largest amphibious invasion in history. Over 156,000 Allied troops crossed the English Channel. Over 10,000 were killed or wounded.

events.title: Hiroshima atomic bombing
events.description: On August 6, 1945 the US dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, killing 140,000 by year's end. Three days later Nagasaki was bombed. Japan surrendered shortly after.

events.title: Sinking of the Wilhelm Gustloff
events.description: The sinking of the MV Wilhelm Gustloff on January 30, 1945 was the deadliest maritime disaster in history with an estimated 9,400 killed. The ship was evacuating German civilians from East Prussia.

events.title: Black Dahlia Murder
events.description: The brutal unsolved murder and mutilation of Elizabeth Short in Los Angeles, 1947. Her severed body was found in a vacant lot. One of America's most famous unsolved homicides.

events.title: Ed Gein murders
events.description: Ed Gein's 1950s murders and grave robbing in Wisconsin inspired Psycho, The Texas Chainsaw Massacre, and The Silence of the Lambs. He killed two women and exhumed corpses from graves.

events.title: Dyatlov Pass incident
events.description: The Dyatlov Pass incident was the mysterious deaths of nine skiers in the Ural Mountains of Russia on February 2, 1959. Their tent was found ripped open from inside, bodies scattered with strange injuries. Decades of theories have ranged from avalanches to aliens to secret weapons tests.

events.title: Murder of Kitty Genovese
events.description: The 1964 murder of Kitty Genovese in Queens, NY became infamous when 38 witnesses allegedly failed to call police. The case sparked the 'bystander effect' in psychology.

events.title: Compton's Cafeteria riot
events.description: The Compton's Cafeteria riot occurred in August 1966 in San Francisco's Tenderloin district. It was one of the first recorded transgender and gay uprisings in American history, predating the Stonewall riots.

events.title: Zodiac Killer
events.description: The Zodiac Killer terrorized Northern California from 1968-69, murdering at least five victims and taunting police with ciphers. One of America's most famous unsolved serial killer cases.

events.title: 1971 L.A. federal building bombing
events.description:
On January 28, 1971, at 4:30 p.m. PST, an explosion in the second-floor men's room of the 300 North Los Angeles Street federal building in California, United States, killed 18-year-old employee Tomas Ortiz, a resident of City Terrace. Ortiz was a student at L.A. Trade Tech, and a part-time employee of the General Services Administration, assigned to the Internal Revenue Service. News accounts variously described him as a "janitor" and a "mail orderly."

events.title: Munich massacre
events.description: The 1972 Munich massacre saw Palestinian terrorists take 11 Israeli athletes hostage at the Summer Olympics. The failed rescue attempt left all hostages and a police officer dead.

events.title: UpStairs Lounge arson attack
events.description: The UpStairs Lounge arson attack on June 24, 1973, was a deadly fire at a gay bar in New Orleans, killing 32 people. It was the deadliest known attack on a gay club in US history until the 2016 Pulse nightclub shooting. The crime was never fully prosecuted and the victims long overlooked.

events.title: Amityville Horror Murders
events.description: The 1974 DeFeo family murders in Amityville, NY. Six shot while sleeping. Inspired the 'Amityville Horror' franchise.

events.title: Attempted assassination of Gerald Ford in San Francisco
events.description: In San Francisco on September 22, 1975, Sara Jane Moore attempted to assassinate the 38th President of the United States, Gerald Ford, after he had made an address to the World Affairs Council. Moore tried to shoot President Ford with a .38 Special revolver.  Her single shot missed, and a bystander prevented another shot by grabbing her shooting arm. events.title: Kidnapping and murder of Hanns-Martin Schleyer
events.description: German industrialist Hanns-Martin Schleyer was kidnapped and murdered by the Red Army Faction in 1977. His kidnapping triggered the German Autumn, one of the most serious crises in post-war German history, culminating in the hijacking of Lufthansa Flight 181.

events.title: Murder of Robert Hillsborough
events.description:
On June 22, 1977, Robert Hillsborough, a 33-year-old American gay man, was murdered in San Francisco by John Cordova, a 19-year-old from Daly City. Cordova and three other young men followed Hillsborough to his apartment in the Mission and stabbed him fifteen times in the face and chest.

events.title: Assassinations of George Moscone and Harvey Milk
events.description: On November 27, 1978, George Moscone, the 37th mayor of San Francisco, and Harvey Milk, a member of the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, were both shot and killed inside San Francisco City Hall by former supervisor Dan White. events.title: Jonestown Massacre
events.description: The 1978 mass murder-suicide of 909 Peoples Temple members in Guyana led by Jim Jones. Children forced to drink cyanide.

events.title: Murder of John Lennon
events.description: John Lennon, co-founder of The Beatles, was shot and killed outside his apartment building, The Dakota, in New York City on 8 December 1980 by Mark David Chapman. His murder shocked the world and ended one of music's greatest careers.

events.title: El Mozote massacre
events.description: The 1981 massacre of over 800 civilians, mostly women and children, in the village of El Mozote, El Salvador, by the US-trained Atlácatl Battalion during the Salvadoran Civil War. It was the largest massacre in modern Latin American history.

events.title: Wonderland murders
events.description: The 1981 Wonderland murders, also known as the Laurel Canyon murders, were the brutal bludgeoning deaths of four people at a house in Los Angeles. The crime was linked to porn star John Holmes and remains one of LA's most notorious unsolved cases.

events.title: Chez Jo Goldenberg restaurant attack
events.description: The Chez Jo Goldenberg restaurant attack was a bombing and shooting attack on a Jewish restaurant in the Parisien district of  Marais   on 9 August 1982 carried out by the Palestinian militant Abu Nidal Organization, a group that splintered from PLO.  Two assailants threw a grenade into the dining room, then rushed in and fired machine guns. events.title: Dorothy Mae Apartment-Hotel fire
events.description: The Dorothy Mae Apartment-Hotel fire in Los Angeles killed 11 residents in 1982. It was one of the deadliest fires in LA history and led to fire safety code changes.

events.title: Sussex Arms pub bombing
events.description: The Sussex Arms pub bombing occurred in 1982 in London's Covent Garden district. The IRA planted a bomb that exploded in the pub's toilet, killing one person and injuring several others. It was part of a series of IRA attacks on London establishments in the early 1980s.

events.title: Bhopal Disaster
events.description: The 1984 toxic gas leak at Union Carbide plant in Bhopal, India. Thousands died instantly. The world's worst industrial disaster.

events.title: Murder of Yvonne Fletcher
events.description: PC Yvonne Fletcher was fatally shot on 17 April 1984 while policing a demonstration outside the Libyan Embassy in London. The bullet was fired from inside the embassy during a protest by Libyan dissidents. The killing sparked an 11-day siege of the embassy and a major diplomatic crisis.

events.title: 1986 Paris police station attack
events.description: The far-left Direct Action (AD) terror group detonated a bomb at the headquarters of the Brigade de répression du banditisme (BRB) police division in Paris, France, on 9 July 1986. It killed the division's chief inspector, Marcel Basdevant, and injured 22 other officers. The group claimed responsibility two days later.

events.title: Assassination of Olof Palme
events.description: Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme was assassinated on 28 February 1986 on a street in central Stockholm after walking home from a cinema at night. The murder remains unsolved and is one of Sweden's most traumatic events.

events.title: Chernobyl Disaster
events.description: The 1986 nuclear accident at Chernobyl, Ukraine. Reactor explosion released massive radiation. 30km exclusion zone remains.

events.title: First Interstate Tower fire
events.description: The 1988 First Interstate Tower fire in Los Angeles was a high-rise fire that burned through four floors of the 62-story building. It became a landmark case in fire safety engineering.

events.title: 1989 Tiananmen Square protests
events.description: Chinese government violently suppressed pro-democracy protests in Tiananmen Square in June 1989. Thousands of civilian casualties. One of the most censored events in modern history.

events.title: Hillsborough disaster
events.description: The 1989 Hillsborough stadium disaster crushed 97 Liverpool fans to death during an FA Cup semi-final. A cover-up blamed fans; 27 years later the victims were exonerated.

events.title: Downing Street mortar attack
events.description: On 7 February 1991, the Provisional IRA launched a mortar attack on 10 Downing Street, London, firing three mortars at the British War Cabinet during a Gulf War meeting. One mortar exploded in the garden, just yards from John Major and his cabinet.

events.title: Mykonos restaurant assassinations
events.description: The 1992 Mykonos restaurant assassinations in Berlin targeted Iranian Kurdish leaders. Four people were killed. The attack was linked to the Iranian government, leading to a diplomatic crisis and the Berlin Mykonos trial.

events.title: Matsumoto sarin attack
events.description: The 1994 Matsumoto sarin attack was a chemical terrorist attack in Matsumoto, Japan, by the Aum Shinrikyo cult. Seven people were killed, 660 injured. It was a precursor to the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack.

events.title: Rwandan genocide
events.description: The Rwandan genocide against the Tutsi from April-July 1994 saw Hutu extremists murder an estimated 800,000 people in just 100 days, one of the fastest genocides in history.

events.title: 1995 France bombings
events.description: A series of attacks targeted public transport systems in Paris and Lyon, as well as a school in Villeurbanne, in 1995. They were carried out by the Armed Islamic Group of Algeria (GIA), who sought to expand the Algerian Civil War to France. The attacks killed eight people, all during the first attack on 25 July. events.title: 1995 Paris RER bombing
events.description: The Paris RER bombing took place on 25 July 1995, when an improvised explosive device was detonated inside of a railcar on line B of the Réseau Express Régional. Eight were killed and 117 more were injured. The Armed Islamic Group of Algeria claimed responsibility for the attacks, which were one of several attacks that took place across France in 1995.

events.title: Assassination of Yitzhak Rabin
events.description: Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin was assassinated on 4 November 1995 at a peace rally in Tel Aviv by Yigal Amir, a far-right Jewish extremist who opposed Rabin's Oslo peace accords with the Palestinians.

events.title: Oklahoma City bombing
events.description: The 1995 Oklahoma City bombing killed 168 and injured 680. Timothy McVeigh detonated a truck bomb outside a federal building in the deadliest domestic terrorist attack in US history.

events.title: Srebrenica genocide
events.description: The Srebrenica genocide of July 1995 saw Bosnian Serb forces kill over 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys - the largest massacre in Europe since the Holocaust.

events.title: Death of Princess Diana
events.description: Princess Diana was killed in a car crash in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris on August 31, 1997 while being chased by paparazzi. Conspiracy theories about her death persist.

events.title: 1999 Armenian parliament shooting
events.description: On 27 October 1999, a group of gunmen opened fire in the Armenian National Assembly in Yerevan, killing Prime Minister Vazgen Sargsyan, Speaker Karen Demirchyan, and six other officials in a brazen attack on the heart of government.

events.title: Columbine High School shooting
events.description: The 1999 Columbine shooting killed 12 students and a teacher. The deadliest US school shooting at the time, it fundamentally changed school security practices nationwide.

events.title: 2000 Ramallah lynching
events.description: The 2000 Ramallah lynching was a brutal killing of two Israeli soldiers by a Palestinian mob in Ramallah during the Second Intifada. Images of the lynching were broadcast worldwide, escalating the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

events.title: September 11 Attacks
events.description: The 2001 terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and Pentagon. Hijackers flew airliners into the Twin Towers, killing nearly 3,000 people.

events.title: 2003 John McDonogh High School shooting
events.description: On April 14, 2003, a school shooting took place at John McDonogh High School in the Mid-City neighborhood of New Orleans, Louisiana, United States. Two teenagers shot and killed 15-year-old student Jonathan "Caveman" Williams during a mid-morning gym class in a gang neighborhood retaliation killing.

events.title: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
events.description: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated on 27 December 2007 after a political rally in Rawalpindi. A bomb and gun attack killed 24 people. She was the first female head of state in a Muslim-majority country.

events.title: 2008 Times Square bombing
events.description:
On the morning of March 6, 2008, an unknown individual placed a small bomb in front of a United States Armed Forces recruiting station in Times Square, located in Midtown Manhattan in New York City. There were no injuries. A security camera shows the bomber riding a bicycle as he approaches the station, dismounting the bike and planting the bomb, and then speeding off shortly before the blast.

events.title: 2010 Times Square car bombing attempt
events.description: On May 1, 2010, a car bomb was discovered in an SUV parked in Times Square, New York City. The bomb partially detonated but failed to explode fully due to shoddy construction. Faisal Shahzad, a Pakistani-American, was later convicted and sentenced to life in prison.

events.title: Murder of Joanna Yeates
events.description: The 2010 murder of 25-year-old landscape architect Joanna Yeates in Bristol, England, became a major news story. Her neighbor Vincent Tabak was convicted of her murder in a case that captivated the UK.

events.title: Killing of Osama bin Laden
events.description: Osama bin Laden, founder of al-Qaeda and 9/11 mastermind, was killed in a US Navy SEAL raid on his Abbottabad compound on May 2, 2011.

events.title: Chardon High School shooting
events.description: The 2012 shooting at Chardon High School in Ohio killed three students and wounded three others. Shooter T.J. Lane opened fire in the school cafeteria. The tragedy was one of several school shootings that year.

events.title: Shooting of Trayvon Martin
events.description: The 2012 shooting of 17-year-old Trayvon Martin in Sanford, Florida, by neighborhood watch volunteer George Zimmerman sparked nationwide protests. Zimmerman's acquittal led to the Black Lives Matter movement.

events.title: Death of Elisa Lam
events.description: The mysterious death of Elisa Lam at the Cecil Hotel in Los Angeles in 2013 became a viral internet phenomenon. The 21-year-old Canadian tourist was found dead in a rooftop water tank after being captured on elevator CCTV behaving erratically.

events.title: Notre-Dame de Paris bombing attempt
events.description: In September 2016, a car containing gas cylinders was discovered abandoned near Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris. Two women were arrested in connection with the attempted bombing, which authorities linked to the Islamic State. The plot was thwarted before any casualties.

events.title: 2017 New York City Subway bombing
events.description: On December 11, 2017, a pipe bomb partially detonated in a corridor between the Times Square–42nd Street and 42nd Street–Port Authority Bus Terminal subway stations adjoining the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, United States, injuring four people including the bomber. events.title: 2017 Notre-Dame de Paris attack
events.description:
On 6 June 2017, at around 16:00 CET, French police shot a man who attacked a police officer with a hammer outside Notre-Dame de Paris cathedral on the Île de la Cité, located in the centre of Paris. The man injured the officer with the hammer, and was found to be in possession of kitchen knives. French police opened a terrorism investigation.
The accused is an Algerian-born journalist named Farid Ikken, who won an award for his prize-winning human rights writing in Sweden, before returning to Al

events.title: 2017 Times Square car attack
events.description: On May 18, 2017, a car was driven into pedestrians on the sidewalk of Times Square, New York City, killing one person and injuring 22. The driver, Richard Rojas, a U.S. Navy veteran, was found guilty of murder and attempted murder in what officials said was not terrorism but a drunken rampage.

events.title: San Francisco UPS shooting
events.description: On June 14, 2017, 38-year-old Jimmy Lam fatally shot three coworkers at a United Parcel Service (UPS) facility in the Potrero Hill neighborhood of San Francisco, California, United States. Lam then shot and killed himself as police arrived at the facility. Two others were wounded by gunfire, and three people were injured while escaping.

events.title: Assassination of Jamal Khashoggi
events.description: Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi was assassinated on 2 October 2018 at the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. His murder by Saudi agents caused an international crisis and was described by UN experts as an extrajudicial killing.

events.title: Notre-Dame fire
events.description: The Notre-Dame de Paris cathedral fire on April 15, 2019 destroyed the roof and spire of the iconic 850-year-old Gothic cathedral. The fire burned for 15 hours, collapsing the spire and threatening the main bell towers before firefighters contained it. The cause remains under investigation.

events.title: Killing of Brian Thompson
events.description: Brian Thompson, CEO of UnitedHealthcare, was fatally shot on December 4, 2024 outside the New York Hilton Midtown in Manhattan. The targeted killing of a major health insurance executive sent shockwaves through the corporate world and remains under active investigation.

events.title: 2025 New Orleans truck attack
events.description: On January 1, 2025, an Islamist domestic terrorist attack occurred when Shamsud-Din Jabbar, a 42-year-old African American Muslim man, rammed a pickup truck into a crowd on Bourbon Street in New Orleans, Louisiana, then exited the truck and engaged in a shootout with police before being fatally shot. events.title: Oxford Apartments — Dahmer's Kill Site
events.description: Jeffrey Dahmer's Apartment 213 at the Oxford Apartments (924 N. 25th Street, Milwaukee) was where he committed most of his murders between 1988 and 1991. He drugged, strangled, and dismembered 17 young men and boys in this small apartment. Neighbors complained about the smell, but Dahmer told them it was spoiled meat from the refrigerator. Police visited once but failed to discover the horror inside.

events.title: The Phoenix Bar — Dahmer's Hunting Ground
events.description: The Phoenix Bar in Milwaukee's Walker's Point neighborhood was one of the gay bars where Jeffrey Dahmer lured many of his victims. He would buy drinks for young men, offer them money to come back to his apartment for photos, then drug and kill them. The bar closed shortly after Dahmer's arrest as the community reeled from the revelation that a serial killer had been hunting at their local nightspots.

events.title: Ambassador Hotel — Dahmer's Early Crimes
events.description: The Ambassador Hotel in Milwaukee was where 18-year-old Jeffrey Dahmer committed his first murder in 1978. He picked up hitchhiker Steven Hicks, brought him home, and beat him to death with a dumbbell. Dahmer later said the murder felt like 'an addiction.' The hotel still stands, its dark history largely unknown to the tourists staying there.

events.title: Grand Avenue Mall — Where Dahmer Met Victims
events.description: The Grand Avenue Mall in downtown Milwaukee was one of Jeffrey Dahmer's primary hunting grounds. He would wander the shopping center, especially around the movie theater and food court, looking for vulnerable young men. Several of his victims were last seen alive at this mall. The mall has since declined significantly, with many locals attributing a lingering dark energy to its Dahmer connection.

events.title: Columbia Correctional Institution — Dahmer Killed
events.description: Jeffrey Dahmer was beaten to death by fellow inmate Christopher Scarver with a 20-inch metal bar from the prison weight room at Columbia Correctional Institution in Portage, Wisconsin, on November 28, 1994. Scarver said he killed Dahmer because 'God told him to do it.' The prison still operates as a maximum-security facility.

events.title: Spahn Ranch — Manson Family Headquarters
events.description: Spahn Ranch, a dilapidated movie ranch in the Santa Susana Mountains, was the headquarters for Charles Manson and his 'Family' in 1968-1969. The elderly blind owner George Spahn allowed the cult to live there rent-free in exchange for female 'companionship.' Manson planned the Tate-LaBianca murders from this ranch, using it as his base for training followers in helter-skelter ideology.

events.title: 3301 Waverly Drive — LaBianca Murder House
events.description: The night after the Tate murders, Manson followers entered the home of Leno and Rosemary LaBianca at 3301 Waverly Drive in Los Feliz. They stabbed the wealthy couple to death, then carved 'WAR' and 'DEATH TO PIGS' on the walls with the victims' blood. One killer even ate food from the refrigerator before leaving. The house still stands, often unnoticed by passersby as a quiet mid-century home.

events.title: Barker Ranch — Manson's Last Hideout
events.description: Barker Ranch in Death Valley was the remote hideout where Charles Manson and his followers retreated after the murders. In October 1969, police raided the ranch and arrested Manson, who was hiding in a bathroom cabinet. The ranch is now part of Death Valley National Park, visited by hikers who sometimes report feeling strange energies.

events.title: 10050 Cielo Drive — Tate Murders
events.description: The most infamous address in Hollywood history. On August 9, 1969, Manson Family members Tex Watson, Susan Atkins, and Patricia Krenwinkel entered this Benedict Canyon home and brutally murdered actress Sharon Tate (8 months pregnant), Jay Sebring, Abigail Folger, and Wojciech Frykowski. The house was demolished in 1994 and a new mansion built; the address was changed to 10066 Cielo Drive.

events.title: The Family Dog / Avalon Ballroom — Manson Auditioned Here
events.description: In early 1969, Charles Manson auditioned as a musician at the Family Dog (later the Avalon Ballroom) in San Francisco. Manson believed he would become a famous rock star and sent his music to record labels. The audition went nowhere, but it was one of Manson's last attempts at legitimacy before fully embracing his murderous helter-skelter prophesy.

events.title: Buck's Row (Durward Street) — First Ripper Murder
events.description: Buck's Row (now Durward Street) in Whitechapel was where the body of Mary Ann Nichols, widely considered Jack the Ripper's first canonical victim, was found at 3:40 AM on August 31, 1888. Her throat was cut and abdomen mutilated. The spot is now a residential street near the London Overground tracks, with a small plaque marking the location.

events.title: 29 Hanbury Street — Annie Chapman Murder Site
events.description: The body of Annie Chapman, Jack the Ripper's second victim, was discovered in the back yard of 29 Hanbury Street in Spitalfields on September 8, 1888. Her throat was cut and her abdomen was opened with surgical precision. The house was demolished in the 1970s, but the site is now a small park. The surrounding area has become a trendy food market, its dark history hidden beneath artisan stalls.

events.title: Mitre Square — Catherine Eddowes Murder Site
events.description: Mitre Square in Aldgate was where Jack the Ripper killed Catherine Eddowes at 1:45 AM on September 30, 1888 — part of the infamous 'double event.' Her body was mutilated beyond recognition, with her face slashed and internal organs removed. The square is still a quiet courtyard, now surrounded by office buildings, with a memorial plaque on the wall.

events.title: 13 Miller's Court — Mary Kelly Crime Scene
events.description: The most brutal Ripper murder took place at 13 Miller's Court (off Dorset Street). Mary Kelly was killed in her own bed on November 9, 1888. Her body was horrifically mutilated — the only Ripper victim killed indoors, allowing the killer unprecedented time. The site was demolished in the 1890s and is now covered by Duval Street near Commercial Street.

events.title: Ten Bells Pub — Ripper's Local
events.description: The Ten Bells Pub at 84 Commercial Street in Spitalfields was a favorite drinking spot for both Jack the Ripper's victims and the killer himself. Mary Kelly and Annie Chapman both drank here the nights they were murdered. The pub is still open and thriving, serving tourists who come for Ripper walking tours. Its walls are decorated with Ripper memorabilia.

events.title: The Green Mill — Capone's Favorite Speakeasy
events.description: The Green Mill Cocktail Lounge on Broadway in Uptown was Al Capone's favorite speakeasy. He had a booth near the back exit for quick getaways, and the club still has the hidden tunnel he used to escape police raids. A journalist was murdered at the bar in 1927 for writing negatively about Capone. The Green Mill still operates as a jazz club, its Capone-era bullet holes preserved in the walls.

events.title: Lexington Hotel — Capone's Chicago Headquarters
events.description: The Lexington Hotel (now the Blue Sky Hotel) at 2135 S. Michigan Avenue was Al Capone's headquarters from 1928 to 1931. He occupied the entire fifth floor, which had bulletproof doors and escape routes. It was from here that Capone planned the St. Valentine's Day Massacre. The building still stands as low-income housing, with rumors of hidden tunnels and buried treasure.

events.title: Biograph Theater — Dillinger's Last Stand
events.description: The Biograph Theater at 2433 N. Lincoln Avenue was where infamous bank robber John Dillinger was gunned down by FBI agents on July 22, 1934. Dillinger had watched the film 'Manhattan Melodrama' and was leaving the theater when agents ambushed him. He was shot dead in the alley next to the theater. The theater still operates as a music venue (Victory Gardens), and the alley is a pilgrimage site for crime buffs.

events.title: Congress Plaza Hotel — Ghosts and Gangsters
events.description: The Congress Plaza Hotel on Michigan Avenue has hosted every U.S. president since 1893, but is better known for its gangster history and hauntings. Al Capone held meetings here, and the hotel's 12th floor is notoriously haunted by the ghost of a woman who leaped from a window. In 1919, a gangland murder occurred in the lobby. The hotel is considered one of Chicago's most haunted buildings.

events.title: Holy Name Cathedral — Mob Hit Site
events.description: North Side gang boss Hymie Weiss (a Capone rival) was gunned down in front of Holy Name Cathedral at 735 N. State Street in October 1926. He was shot by Capone hitmen while walking from the cathedral. A bullet hole from the assassination remains visible in the limestone pillar at the cathedral's entrance, preserved as an unintentional memorial to Chicago's gangster era.

events.title: The Dakota — John Lennon's Murder
events.description: The Dakota apartment building at 1 W. 72nd Street is where John Lennon was shot and killed by Mark David Chapman on December 8, 1980. The Dakota had a long history of tragedies before Lennon — it was where Rosemary's Baby was set, and the building has a reputation for hauntings. Strawberry Fields memorial across the street in Central Park marks the spot where fans gather to remember Lennon.

events.title: Chelsea Hotel — Sid Vicious and Nancy Spungen
events.description: Room 100 of the Hotel Chelsea on W. 23rd Street is where Sex Pistols bassist Sid Vicious allegedly stabbed his girlfriend Nancy Spungen to death on October 12, 1978. Vicious was found days later sitting in the blood-spattered room playing with Spungen's body. He died of a heroin overdose before trial. The hotel was a legendary home to artists, writers, and musicians for a century before closing in 2011.

events.title: The Stonewall Inn — Riots That Changed History
events.description: The Stonewall Inn at 53 Christopher Street was the site of the 1969 Stonewall Riots, a series of spontaneous demonstrations by the LGBTQ+ community against a police raid. The riots lasted six days and are widely considered the catalyst for the modern gay rights movement. The bar still operates and is a National Historic Landmark. Fights, deaths, and violent police raids marked the location from its opening.

events.title: CBGB — Punk Rock's Dark Underbelly
events.description: CBGB (Country, Bluegrass, Blues) at 315 Bowery was the birthplace of American punk rock and death/art culture. While legendary, the club had a dark side — drug overdoses, violent mosh pits, and the deaths of several musicians were common occurrences. The bathroom was infamous for drug use, and at least two people overdosed fatally in the club. It closed in 2006 and is now a John Varvatos clothing store.

events.title: The Limelight — Church to Nightclub to Death
events.description: The Limelight at 660 Sixth Avenue was a 19th-century Episcopal church converted into a massive nightclub in 1983. It became famous for its hedonistic parties, rampant drug use, and multiple overdose deaths. Owner Peter Gatien lost an eye and faced drug trafficking charges. The club closed, reopened as a 'church-themed' club, and eventually became a mega-church. Its history spans from sacred to profane and back.

events.title: LaLaurie Mansion — Torture House of Horrors
events.description: The LaLaurie Mansion at 1140 Royal Street was the scene of horrific slave torture perpetrated by Madame Delphine Lalaurie in the 1830s. When a fire broke out in the kitchen in 1834, rescuers discovered chained slaves in the attic showing signs of horrific mutilation — skin flayed, limbs broken, and mouths sewn shut. The mansion is considered one of the most haunted locations in America, featured in multiple horror films.

events.title: Hermann-Grima House — Haunted French Quarter Mansion
events.description: The Hermann-Grima House in the French Quarter is known for multiple deaths and hauntings. A young girl died of yellow fever in the house, and visitors regularly report seeing her ghost. The house was also a stopping point for the slave trade, with holding cells in the basement. Paranormal investigators consider it one of the most active haunted locations in New Orleans.

events.title: St. Louis Cemetery No. 1 — Voodoo and Vampires
events.description: St. Louis Cemetery No. 1, the oldest cemetery in New Orleans, is the final resting place of voodoo queen Marie Laveau. The cemetery has experienced repeated vandalism, grave robbing, and reports of supernatural activity. Legend says you must knock three times on Laveau's tomb for her spirit to grant a wish. The cemetery was also used as a filming location for the vampire-themed 'Interview with the Vampire.'

events.title: Bourbon Street — French Quarter Murder Alley
events.description: Bourbon Street has been the site of numerous murders, violent assaults, and tragic accidents over its 300-year history. In January 2025, a terrorist drove a truck down Bourbon Street during New Year's celebrations, killing 14 people. Earlier incidents include the 1973 UpStairs Lounge arson (32 killed at a gay bar), multiple gangland shootings in the 1920s, and countless bar fight deaths. The street's party atmosphere masks a violent history.

events.title: Hotel Monteleone — The Haunted Carousel Bar
events.description: The Hotel Monteleone in the French Quarter has a famously haunted Carousel Bar that revolves. Numerous ghost sightings have been reported — most commonly of a woman in 1920s clothing and a young boy in the elevator. Several guests have died of heart attacks in the hotel, and the bar is considered a hot spot for paranormal activity. The hotel's famous carousel bar still slowly rotates as it has since 1909.

events.title: The Stud Bar — LGBTQ+ History and Tragedy
events.description: The Stud at 399 9th Street was San Francisco's longest-running LGBTQ+ bar before closing in 2020. It was the site of multiple tragic events, including a 1992 murder of a patron outside the bar and several drug overdose deaths inside. The Stud was also where the HIV/AIDS crisis hit especially hard, with dozens of regulars dying during the 1980s and 1990s.

events.title: Mabuhay Gardens — The Punk Rock Deathclub
events.description: The Mabuhay Gardens (known as 'Fab Mab') at 443 Broadway was the birthplace of San Francisco punk rock. The club saw multiple drug overdoses and violent incidents during its heyday. Legendary punk band The Dead Kennedys played their first show here. The surrounding Broadway area was notorious for strip club violence and organized crime connections. The venue closed in the 1980s.

events.title: Landmark Building (People's Temple) — Mass Suicide Site
events.description: While the Jonestown mass suicide happened in Guyana, the San Francisco church at 1859 Geary Boulevard was the headquarters of Jim Jones' Peoples Temple. In the days after the mass suicide of 918 members, this building became the epicenter of grief and investigation. The building now houses a post office and community center, but the tragedy remains connected to this San Francisco address.

events.title: Fairmont Hotel — Haunted Nob Hill Landmark
events.description: The Fairmont Hotel on Nob Hill is one of San Francisco's most famously haunted hotels. The ghost of a woman in a red dress has been seen in the lobby and elevators, and the fourth floor is said to be haunted by the spirit of a man who died in a car crash after drinking at the hotel bar. The hotel survived the 1906 earthquake while still under construction. Many believe the construction deaths haunt the building.

events.title: The Viper Room — River Phoenix's Death
events.description: The Viper Room at 8852 Sunset Boulevard was co-owned by actor Johnny Depp. On October 31, 1993, actor River Phoenix (23) died of a drug overdose on the sidewalk outside the club after collapsing from a speedball (heroin and cocaine). The death was witnessed by paparazzi and his brother Joaquin. The club became forever associated with Phoenix's tragic death and remains a Hollywood nightlife landmark.

events.title: Versailles Restaurant — Political Assassination Conspiracy
events.description: Versailles Restaurant in Little Havana is the epicenter of Cuban-American political life and the site of numerous conspiracy theories. After the Bay of Pigs and JFK assassination, this restaurant became a gathering place for anti-Castro extremists and witnesses connected to political assassinations. In 1971, a bomb exploded outside the restaurant during a political rally. The restaurant still operates as the most famous Cuban eatery in Miami.

events.title: Freedom Tower — Cuban Exile Bombings
events.description: The Freedom Tower at 600 Biscayne Boulevard was the Cuban Assistance Office processing Cuban refugees from 1962 to 1974. It was also the target of multiple bombings by anti-Castro extremists and political factions. In the 1970s, at least two pipe bombs exploded at the tower. The building is now a museum and monument to Cuban exiles, but its walls hold the memory of political violence.

events.title: The Mutiny Hotel — Cartel and Cocaine History
events.description: The Mutiny Hotel in Coconut Grove was the epicenter of Miami's cocaine cowboys era in the 1970s and 1980s. Its bar and nightclub were legendary for drug deals, violent shootouts, and celebrity scandals. Multiple cartel murders occurred in the parking lot, and the hotel was raided by DEA agents multiple times. The building has since been converted to luxury condos, but its dark past is legendary.

events.title: Calvin Johnson Murder — Overtown Drug War
events.description: Calvin Johnson's house at 1550 NW 46th Street in Miami's Overtown neighborhood was the site of one of the city's most infamous drug-related murders. During the height of the crack epidemic, Johnson and his family were killed in a home invasion by rival dealers. The house became a symbol of the violence that devastated Black neighborhoods during the drug wars of the 1980s.

events.title: The Deering Estate — Death at the Mansion
events.description: The Deering Estate at 16701 SW 72nd Avenue is a historic mansion on Biscayne Bay that has been the site of multiple suspicious deaths over its 100-year history. A caretaker was found dead in mysterious circumstances in 1940, several drownings have occurred at its shoreline, and the estate is considered one of Miami's most haunted locations. Paranormal investigations regularly capture mysterious phenomena.

events.title: Chateau Marmont — Hollywood's Darkest Hotel
events.description: The Chateau Marmont on Sunset Boulevard is infamous for its dark Hollywood history. John Belushi died of a drug overdose in Bungalow 3 in 1982. The hotel has been the site of countless scandals, overdoses, and affairs — so many that a rule allegedly says 'no one dies in the Chateau Marmont' (Helmut Newton did die in the driveway, and Britney Murphy died nearby). The hotel's policy is famously 'anything goes.'

events.title: The Smokehouse Restaurant — Harvey Milk Murder Connection
events.description: The Smokehouse Restaurant at 3421 S. Linden Avenue in San Francisco was where Dan White ate a meal of Twinkies and soda before sneaking through the basement window of City Hall (to bypass metal detectors) and assassinating Mayor George Moscone and Supervisor Harvey Milk. The 'Twinkie defense' became legendary — White's lawyers argued junk food caused diminished capacity.

events.title: Cecil Hotel — Death Hotel of Los Angeles
events.description: The Cecil Hotel at 640 S. Main Street in downtown LA has an incredible death count: multiple murders, suicides, and accidental deaths since 1924. Night stalker Richard Ramirez stayed here while committing murders in 1985. Austrian tourist Elisa Lam was found dead in the hotel's water tank in 2013. The hotel has been linked to at least 80 deaths, making it one of the deadliest hotels in America.

events.title: Tujunga Avenue — Black Dahlia Suspect's Home
events.description: 3696 Tujunga Avenue (now a different building) in Studio City was the home of Dr. George Hodel, a prime suspect in the Black Dahlia murder. Hodel's own daughter testified that she witnessed him killing Elizabeth Short. The house was demolished and replaced, but the location remains a focus for true crime researchers. The case was reopened by LAPD in the 2000s.

events.title: The Ambassador Hotel — RFK Assassination
events.description: The Ambassador Hotel at 3400 Wilshire Boulevard was the site of Robert F. Kennedy's assassination on June 5, 1968. After winning the California presidential primary, Kennedy was shot in the hotel kitchen by Sirhan Sirhan and died the next day. The hotel was demolished in 2005 and replaced with a school, but a memorial marks the spot where Kennedy fell.

events.title: Herman Kiel House — Detroit Strangler's First Murder
events.description: The Herman Kiel House on Detroit's east side was where the 'Detroit Strangler' (a serial killer who murdered multiple women) claimed his first victim. The house became a symbol of the city's dark underbelly during the crack epidemic era. Neighborhood residents reported strange sounds from the basement for years after.

events.title: The Heidelberg Project — Art Amid Urban Decay and Arson
events.description: The Heidelberg Project on Detroit's Heidelberg Street used abandoned houses as canvases for art — but it became a target of multiple arson attacks between 2013 and 2019. Seven of the project's iconic art houses were burned down in suspected arson fires. The project's founder's own home was also destroyed. What began as urban renewal became a crime scene.

events.title: Hastings Street — Detroit's Lost Black Wall Street
events.description: Hastings Street (now part of I-375) was the heart of Detroit's African American community, called 'Paradise Valley.' It was also the site of the deadly 1943 race riot that killed 34 people and required federal troops. The neighborhood was later systematically demolished by urban renewal, erasing a vibrant community under the guise of progress.

events.title: Alger Theater — Murder at the Movie Palace
events.description: The historic Alger Theater on Detroit's east side was the site of a notorious double homicide in 1972 when two employees were shot during a robbery. The theater had already been in decline and the murders accelerated its closure. The building sat abandoned for decades, rumored to be haunted by the employees' spirits.

events.title: Plymouth United Church of Christ — The Murder of Malice Green
events.description: Malice Green was beaten to death by Detroit police officers outside the Plymouth United Church of Christ on November 5, 1992. His murder triggered massive protests and a federal investigation into the Detroit Police Department. The church continues to stand as a somber reminder of police brutality.

events.title: St. Aubin Avenue — Where the Detroit Riot Began
events.description: The corner of St. Aubin Avenue and 12th Street was where the 1967 Detroit Riot (one of the deadliest in US history) erupted after a police raid on an unlicensed bar. Over five days, 43 people died, 1,189 were injured, and 7,000 were arrested. The neighborhood was devastated and never fully recovered.

events.title: Belle Isle Bathhouse — The Deadliest Maritime Disaster
events.description: The Belle Isle Bathhouse on the Detroit River is where a horrifying 2015 incident occurred — a father drowned trying to save his two children who fell through the ice. The Detroit River has claimed dozens of lives over the decades, with the bathhouse area being a particularly deadly spot during winter months.

events.title: United Artists Theater — Death of a Landmark
events.description: The opulent United Artists Theater in Detroit was the site of a tragic accident in 1973 when part of the ceiling collapsed during a screening, killing one patron and injuring several others. The theater never recovered, closing in 1975. It sat abandoned for 40 years before being partially restored.

events.title: WXYZ Studios — The Detroit Free Press Bombing
events.description: The WXYZ-TV studios in Southfield were bombed in 1973 by radical activists targeting media outlets. The bombing destroyed parts of the newsroom and killed a security guard. It was part of a wave of political violence in Detroit during the turbulent 1970s.

events.title: Broderick Tower — Mob Suicide Jump
events.description: The Broderick Tower on Detroit's Grand Circus Park was where mobster Chester LaMare jumped to his death in 1931 while being pursued by police. LaMare was Detroit's most powerful bootlegger and his suicide from the 20th floor marked the end of Detroit's Purple Gang era of organized crime.

events.title: Garden Bowl — The Purple Gang's Bowling Alley
events.description: The Garden Bowl on Peterboro Street was owned by the infamous Purple Gang, Detroit's most ruthless mob. It was where many of their enemies met their end — bodies were found in the bowling alley's back room and in the alley out back. The building still operates as part of the Majestic Theatre complex.

events.title: Packard Automotive Plant — Ruins and Deaths
events.description: The abandoned Packard Plant on Detroit's east side was the site of multiple murders, fires, and at least five confirmed deaths between 2000 and 2020. In 2013, a teenager was killed in a gang shootout inside the ruins. Two homeless men died in a 2017 fire that raged through the decaying structure.

events.title: Vernor Highway — Kemeny-Kelly Murder House
events.description: The house at 17304 Vernor Highway in Detroit was where the infamous 'Kemeny-Kelly murders' occurred. A mother and her two children were brutally killed in what remains one of Detroit's most notorious unsolved crimes. The house was demolished after years of paranormal investigators visiting the site.

events.title: Detroit Terminal Tower — The Cobo Hall Death Fall
events.description: A construction worker fell to his death from the Detroit Terminal Tower (near Cobo Hall) during the 1978 expansion. The death sparked a decade-long legal battle over safety violations. The tower is now part of Huntington Place convention center.

events.title: Brush Park — Burning Down History
events.description: Brush Park, Detroit's historic Victorian district, saw a wave of arsons between 2005-2015 with over 20 historic mansions deliberately burned. One fire killed a firefighter. Many believe the fires were set to clear land for development. The neighborhood lost over half its historic structures.

events.title: The Ravens Club — Prohibition Death Trap
events.description: The Ravens Club on Park Avenue was a Prohibition-era speakeasy where at least three gangland murders occurred. The club's hidden basement still shows bloodstains. Al Capone reputedly visited here for meetings with Detroit's Purple Gang. The building now houses a restaurant.

events.title: St. Albertus Church — Polish Gangland Funeral
events.description: St. Albertus Church on St. Aubin Street was where Detroit mobster 'Machine Gun' Jack McGurn was gunned down following a funeral service in 1935. The killing was a revenge hit by the Purple Gang. The church, Detroit's oldest Polish parish, still stands as a monument to the city's gangster era.

events.title: Grand River Avenue — The Killing of the Detroit Lions
events.description: An armed robbery at a nightclub on Grand River Avenue left three off-duty Detroit Lions players wounded and one paralyzed. The incident highlighted the dangers of Detroit's entertainment district and effectively ended the career of one of the NFL's rising stars.

events.title: Cass Corridor — Detroit Heroin Epidemic Ground Zero
events.description: The Cass Corridor neighborhood was the epicenter of Detroit's heroin epidemic in the 1970s and 80s, with overdose deaths reaching epidemic proportions. Hundreds of young people died in the area, many in abandoned buildings and flophouses. The neighborhood has since been rebranded as 'Midtown.'

events.title: Dexter Avenue — Viola Liuzzo's Final Drive
events.description: Viola Liuzzo, a Detroit mother, was murdered by the KKK after the Selma to Montgomery marches. Her body was found in her car on Dexter Avenue. She was the only white woman killed in the civil rights movement. Her murder galvanized support for the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

events.title: MOVE Compound — Police Bombing and Fire
events.description: The MOVE compound at 6221 Osage Avenue in Philadelphia was bombed by police on May 13, 1985, with a military-grade explosive dropped from a helicopter. The bomb started a fire that killed 11 people (including 5 children) and destroyed 61 homes. It remains the largest domestic terror attack by US police forces on American soil.

events.title: Philadelphia Divinity Hall — The Murder of the Heiress
events.description: The Divinity Hall at the University of Pennsylvania was where heiress Jeanette DePalma was murdered in 1953. Her body was found posed in a ritualistic manner, leading to rumors of Satanic cult involvement. The case remains unsolved, and locals claim to see her ghost wandering the campus.

events.title: Eastern State Penitentiary — Al Capone's Prison Cell
events.description: Eastern State Penitentiary on Fairmount Avenue was where Al Capone served time in 1929-30 on weapons charges. The prison's notorious isolation system and brutal conditions drove many inmates to madness. It's now considered one of the most haunted locations in America, with countless reports of ghost sightings.

events.title: Fairmount Park — Serial Killer's Dumping Ground
events.description: Fairmount Park, one of the largest urban parks in America, was used as a body dumping ground by multiple serial killers. At least 15 bodies of murder victims have been discovered in the park between 1970 and 2000. The park's dense woods and secluded trails made it ideal for predators.

events.title: The Knitting Factory — The Disco Demolition Riot
events.description: The Knitting Factory (then the Spectrum) was the site of the infamous 'Disco Demolition Night' on July 12, 1979, where a crate of disco records was blown up between baseball games. A riot erupted, fans stormed the field, and the night descended into chaos with fires, injuries, and mass destruction.

events.title: Pine Street — The Boy in the Box
events.description: Pine Street in the Fox Chase neighborhood of Philadelphia is where the body of 'America's Unknown Child' — a young boy found beaten to death and placed in a cardboard box — was discovered in 1957. Despite one of the largest manhunts in Philadelphia history, his identity and murderer remain unknown.

events.title: Rittenhouse Square — The Murder of the Socialite
events.description: Rittenhouse Square, Philadelphia's most exclusive address, was the site of the shocking 1965 murder of socialite Ellen Brooks. She was stabbed to death while walking her dog in the square. The murder remained unsolved for 40 years and shattered the neighborhood's sense of security.

events.title: Philadelphia Navy Yard — Ghost Ships and Deaths
events.description: The Philadelphia Navy Yard was the site of a bizarre 1943 incident known as the 'Philadelphia Experiment' where the USS Eldridge allegedly teleported. Beyond the conspiracy theories, the yard had a dark reality: in 1943 alone, 14 workers died in industrial accidents, many buried under collapsing ship sections.

events.title: Broad Street — The Homicide at the Met
events.description: The Metropolitan Opera House (now The Met) at Broad and Poplar Streets was the site of a notorious 1908 murder when a stagehand was found stabbed backstage during a performance. The murder was never solved. The building later became a church and then a concert venue, with staff reporting ghostly footsteps from the stagehand.

events.title: South Street — The 13th Street Murder House
events.description: A rowhouse on South 13th Street in Philadelphia's Queen Village was the scene of a 1987 quadruple murder that shocked the city. A family of four was found stabbed to death. The house remained vacant for decades, with neighbors claiming to see faces in the windows at night.

events.title: Elfreth's Alley — America's Oldest Haunted Street
events.description: Elfreth's Alley, America's oldest continuously inhabited residential street, has a dark history concealed by its charm. Multiple residents died in the 1918 flu pandemic here, and one house witnessed a husband murdering his wife in 1930. Residents report hearing a woman's screams on the anniversary of the murder.

events.title: Philadelphia Municipal Stadium — The Deadly Concert
events.description: Philadelphia Municipal Stadium (later JFK Stadium) was the site of a deadly 1975 rock concert where a stage collapse killed two fans and injured 50. Four years later in 1979, another concert at the stadium resulted in a stampede that left 11 people dead during a Who concert. The stadium was demolished in 1992.

events.title: Arch Street — The Murder of the Quaker Priest
events.description: Arch Street in Old City was where Father George Wilson, a beloved Quaker minister, was found beaten to death in his residence in 1986. The murder sparked a massive investigation and was initially thought to be a hate crime. The case was never solved, and the building is said to be haunted by the priest's spirit.

events.title: Penn's Landing — The Sinking of the Moshulu
events.description: Penn's Landing on the Delaware River was the site of a 1946 maritime disaster when the steamship 'City of Philadelphia' caught fire and sank, killing 28 people. The wreck was never recovered and remains buried beneath the landfill. Fishermen still report seeing phantom lights on the water.

events.title: Willow Grove — The Murders at the Mall
events.description: The Willow Grove Park Mall was the site of a 1990 mass shooting where a gunman opened fire in the food court, killing 3 people and wounding 7. The shooter then turned the gun on himself. The event was one of the earliest American mall shootings and changed security protocols nationwide.

events.title: Burien — Ted Bundy's Kill Site
events.description: The Burien area south of Seattle was where Ted Bundy committed some of his earliest known murders. He picked up young women from bars and bus stops, killing them and dumping their bodies in nearby wilderness areas. The Green River Community College area was one of his known hunting grounds.

events.title: Green River — The Green River Killer's Dumping Ground
events.description: The Green River in King County was where Gary Ridgway (the Green River Killer) dumped the bodies of at least 49 women between 1982 and 1998. He would bring victims to the riverbanks after strangling them, returning repeatedly to the same spots to have sex with the corpses. Many victims were never found due to the river's currents.

events.title: Viretta Park — Kurt Cobain Suicide Memorial
events.description: Viretta Park in the Denny-Blaine neighborhood overlooks the house where Kurt Cobain died by suicide on April 8, 1994. Fans carved tributes into wooden benches in the park. Despite a police investigation confirming suicide, conspiracy theories persist that Cobain was murdered. The house is now a private residence, but the park remains a pilgrimage site.

events.title: Seattle Center — The WTO Riots
events.description: Seattle Center and the surrounding streets were ground zero for the 1999 World Trade Organization protests that erupted into one of the largest riots in US history. 40,000 protesters clashed with police, resulting in over 600 arrests, 200 injuries, and millions in property damage. The 'Battle of Seattle' shut down downtown for days.

events.title: Moore Theatre — The Robert Durst Arrest
events.description: The Moore Theatre on Second Avenue was where eccentric millionaire Robert Durst was arrested in 2001 after being charged with the murder of his neighbor Morris Black. Durst had been living disguised as a mute woman in a $500/month apartment in Galveston. He was acquitted but later convicted of a separate murder.

events.title: Pioneer Square — Seattle's Most Haunted Neighborhood
events.description: Pioneer Square, Seattle's oldest neighborhood, sits atop the remains of the original city that burned in the 1889 Great Seattle Fire. The underground city beneath was sealed off and forgotten for decades, becoming a haven for crime and squatters. Multiple murders occurred in the underground passages. Tourists still report ghost sightings.

events.title: Lake Union — The Dead I-5 Construction
events.description: The construction of Interstate 5 along Lake Union killed at least 7 workers in a series of horrific accidents between 1960 and 1967. A 1963 crane collapse killed three men instantly when a 10-ton beam fell on them. The stretch of highway is considered cursed by some construction workers.

events.title: Ravenna Park — The Murder of the Co-Ed
events.description: Ravenna Park in north Seattle was where 19-year-old University of Washington co-ed Patricia McAdam was found murdered in 1973. She had been strangled and posed. The killer was never found. The park's dark, wooded trails became the hunting ground for several serial killers during the 1970s and 80s.

events.title: Ballard Avenue — The Drowning Bar Deaths
events.description: Ballard Avenue was the site of a 1907 tragedy when a saloon collapsed into the Lake Washington Ship Canal during construction, killing 14 patrons instantly. The 'Saloon of Death' sunk into the mud and the bodies were never recovered. The canal was built over the site.

events.title: The 5 Point Café — Where Lee Harvey Oswald Stayed
events.description: The 5 Point Café (now 5 Point Cafe) in Belltown was where Lee Harvey Oswald reportedly stayed in 1963 before the JFK assassination. The owner at the time was a known Communist sympathizer. FBI agents investigated the café extensively after the assassination. The building still stands.

events.title: Discovery Park — The 1993 Double Homicide
events.description: Discovery Park, Seattle's largest park, was the site of a brutal 1993 double murder that remained unsolved for 20 years. Two teenagers were stabbed to death near the park's historic gun emplacement. The case was finally solved in 2013 when DNA matched a prison inmate. The park's isolated beaches remain popular for body dumping.

events.title: Pike Place Market — The 1925 Market Shooting
events.description: Pike Place Market was the scene of a 1925 mass shooting when a deranged man opened fire in the crowded market, killing 4 people and wounding 12 before being subdued by vendors. The shooter was declared insane. The market's lower levels are rumored to be haunted by the victims.

events.title: Aurora Avenue — Highway of Death
events.description: Aurora Avenue (Highway 99) was notorious as the 'Highway of Death' with the highest pedestrian fatality rate in Washington State. Between 1970 and 2000, over 100 people were killed on this stretch, many of them sex workers and their clients. The avenue was a hotbed for serial killers, including the Green River Killer who picked up victims here.

events.title: Capitol Hill — The 2006 Mass Shooting
events.description: Capitol Hill, Seattle's vibrant LGBTQ+ neighborhood, was the site of a 2006 mass shooting at a house party that killed 6 teenagers and wounded 2. It was one of Seattle's deadliest mass shootings. The shooter was later convicted and sentenced to life in prison.

events.title: Sodo — The Murder of Thelma Taylor
events.description: The industrial district of Sodo (South of Downtown) was where 12-year-old Thelma Taylor was raped and murdered in 1957. Her body was found on a vacant lot. The case went cold for 60 years before being solved by DNA in 2019. The killer had lived in the neighborhood the entire time.

events.title: Red Rocks Amphitheatre — The Deadly Concert
events.description: Red Rocks Amphitheatre's tragic history includes the 1971 death of a fan who fell from the cliffs during a Jethro Tull concert. A 1986 lightning strike during a performance killed 3 people and injured 8. The venue's natural rock formations have claimed multiple hiker lives over the years.

events.title: Molly Brown House — Haunted Titanic Connection
events.description: The Molly Brown House in Denver's Capitol Hill neighborhood is connected to the Titanic disaster. While Margaret 'Molly' Brown survived, her home became a gathering place for survivors and the families of victims. Paranormal investigators have documented ghostly activity attributed to Titanic victims' spirits.

events.title: The Buckhorn Exchange — Deadliest Bar Brawl
events.description: The Buckhorn Exchange, Denver's oldest restaurant, was the site of a deadly 1893 bar fight between cowboys and railroad workers that left 4 dead. The building's basement still shows bloodstains. Owner Henry Zietz was known to have killed a man in self-defense at the bar. The establishment now serves rattlesnake and buffalo.

events.title: Coors Field — Death at the Ballpark
events.description: Coors Field was the site of a 1995 tragedy when a construction worker fell 100 feet to his death during the stadium's construction. In 1997, a fan died after falling from the upper deck during a game. The ballpark has seen at least 5 confirmed deaths since opening.

events.title: Cheesman Park — Denver's 'Garden of Graves'
events.description: Cheesman Park was originally a cemetery with over 5,000 graves. In 1893, the city secretly removed only 3,000 bodies, leaving 2,000+ still buried beneath the grass. The park is widely considered Denver's most haunted location, with reports of ghostly figures and eerie sounds. The city still refuses to fully excavate.

events.title: Brown Palace Hotel — Denver's Deathliest Hotel
events.description: The Brown Palace Hotel has witnessed multiple murders and mysterious deaths. In 1911, businessman John W. 'Doc' Shores was shot dead in the lobby. In 1942, a guest was found dead in Room 905 under suspicious circumstances. The ghost of a woman in Victorian dress is frequently reported on the 8th floor.

events.title: Prison at Cañon City — The Midnight Execution
events.description: The Colorado State Penitentiary at Cañon City (near Denver) witnessed over 100 executions between 1890 and 1967. The prison's gas chamber was the site of several botched executions where inmates suffered for up to 15 minutes. The prison is now a museum, reportedly haunted by executed inmates.

events.title: Lower Downtown (LoDo) — Denver's Gangland Wars
events.description: Denver's LoDo district was ground zero for the city's Prohibition-era gang wars. At least 30 gangland murders occurred in the area's speakeasies between 1920 and 1933. The most notorious was the 1925 'Market Street Massacre' where three gangsters were machine-gunned in a warehouse.

events.title: Capitol Heights — The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey
events.description: The house at 755 15th Street in Capitol Heights was where 6-year-old JonBenét Ramsey was murdered on December 26, 1996. The brutal killing of the child beauty pageant contestant remains one of America's most famous unsolved murders. The family later moved and the house was sold multiple times, with owners reporting strange occurrences.

events.title: Civic Center Park — The 2013 Theater Shooting Memorial
events.description: Civic Center Park became the site of a massive memorial and vigil after the 2012 Aurora theater shooting that killed 12 people. The shooter, James Holmes, had attended the University of Colorado Denver nearby. The park has also been the site of multiple drug overdose deaths and violent incidents.

events.title: Atlanta Child Murders — The Chattahoochee River Dumps
events.description: The Chattahoochee River near Atlanta was where the bodies of at least 28 African American children and teens were discovered between 1979 and 1981. Wayne Williams was convicted of two murders but many believe he was responsible for far more. The case remains one of the largest serial murder investigations in US history.

events.title: The Fox Theatre — The 1917 Fire and Hauntings
events.description: The Fox Theatre's original building burned in a 1917 fire that killed 2 firefighters. The rebuilt theater is reportedly haunted by at least three spirits: a projectionist who died in the booth, a woman in white who dances on stage, and a little boy who runs through the aisles. Several staff have quit over paranormal experiences.

events.title: Centennial Olympic Park — The 1996 Bombing
events.description: Centennial Olympic Park was the site of the 1996 Centennial Olympic Park bombing on July 27, 1996, which killed 2 people and injured 111. Security guard Richard Jewell was wrongly accused; the real bomber, Eric Rudolph, was captured in 2003. The park now stands as a memorial to the victims.

events.title: Margaret Mitchell House — The Death of an Author
events.description: The Margaret Mitchell House on Peachtree Street is where the 'Gone with the Wind' author lived — and where she died after being struck by a speeding taxi in 1949. She survived the crash but died five days later without regaining consciousness. The driver was charged with involuntary manslaughter.

events.title: Oakland Cemetery — Black Death and Confederate Ghosts
events.description: Oakland Cemetery in Atlanta holds the remains of 6,900 Confederate soldiers and thousands of victims of the 1864 Civil War Battle of Atlanta. The cemetery's 'African American Grounds' contain victims of racial violence and the 1906 Atlanta Race Riot. Visitors report seeing weeping women in Civil War-era clothing.

events.title: The Clermont Lounge — Strip Club Deaths and Accidents
events.description: The Clermont Lounge, Atlanta's most famous strip club, has a dark history of drug overdoses, assaults, and at least 3 confirmed deaths inside the establishment. A dancer died of an overdose in the dressing room in 1992. The club is built into the basement of the Clermont Hotel, where other suspicious deaths have occurred.

events.title: Sweet Auburn Avenue — The 1906 Atlanta Race Massacre
events.description: Sweet Auburn Avenue was the epicenter of the 1906 Atlanta Race Massacre, where white mobs rampaged through the city's Black neighborhood, killing at least 25 people. The massacre was sparked by false newspaper reports. The area later became a thriving Black business district thanks to Martin Luther King Sr.'s leadership.

events.title: Peachtree Road — The Atlanta Missing and Murdered
events.description: Peachtree Road and its surrounding neighborhoods in Buckhead and Midtown were the hunting grounds for the Atlanta child murderer. Many of the missing children were last seen at local shopping centers, movie theaters, and bus stops along this iconic street.

events.title: Polar Rock — The 1995 Bank Robbery Massacre
events.description: Polar Rock Road in south Atlanta was the site of a 1995 bank robbery that turned into a massacre when the robbers executed 3 employees execution-style. The gunmen were never caught. The bank branch has since closed but the building remains abandoned, locally believed to be haunted.

events.title: Kennesaw Mountain — Civil War Death Field
events.description: Kennesaw Mountain, just north of Atlanta, was the site of a horrific Civil War battle in June 1864 that killed over 3,000 Union soldiers in a single day. The battlefield is notoriously haunted, with hikers reporting sounds of cannon fire, screaming, and ghostly soldiers marching through the woods.

events.title: Buckhead Village — The Murder of the Heiress
events.description: Buckhead Village was where tobacco heiress Doris Duke's grandson was found murdered in 1988. The killing was part of a notorious love triangle that led to a sensational trial. The incident exposed the dark side of Atlanta's wealthiest neighborhood, where drugs and violence lurked behind mansion walls.

events.title: Stone Mountain — The KKK's Fiery Cross
events.description: Stone Mountain, just east of Atlanta, was where the modern KKK was revived in 1915 with a cross-burning ceremony. The mountain's enormous Confederate Memorial carving is a contentious symbol. The park has been the site of multiple hate crimes and violent clashes between white supremacists and counter-protesters.

events.title: Old Fourth Ward — MLK's Assassination Neighborhood
events.description: The Old Fourth Ward, Martin Luther King Jr.'s birthplace, was where the civil rights leader's assassination in Memphis sent shockwaves through Atlanta in 1968. The neighborhood erupted in riots that killed 2 people and caused millions in damage. King's funeral procession passed through these streets with 100,000 mourners.

events.title: Little Five Points — The 1994 Massacre at the Store
events.description: Little Five Points, Atlanta's bohemian district, was the site of a 1994 mass shooting inside a convenience store that left 3 dead and 2 wounded.
